sources.citation: Taherkhani, Neda & Scott Nelson. 2024. Southern Tati: Takestani dialect (Illustrations of the IPA). JIPA 54(1): 559-574. doi:10.1017/S0025100323000270
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Takestani (take1255), NOT Razajerdi: 'Stress is contrastive in Takestani words and partly predictable from word class and shape. Stress in nouns is generally ultimate..' (p. 567). Does not mention Razajerd or Kuhpayeh; Stilo 1981 puts Razajerdi in a different group, so not transferred.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Razjerd village website (zeziyard.com), page 'زبان' [Language], quoting Parviz Varjavand, Sarzamin-e Qazvin (Tehran: Anjoman-e Asar-e Melli, 1349/1970) on the speech of Razeh-jerd; plus word-list pages (the Internet Archive 2016 copies)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The quoted Varjavand passage classifies Razeh-jerd speech as the third type of Kuhpayeh Tati and describes gender marking (2nd/3rd person); word lists give Persian glosses with unaccented Latin transliterations (e.g. âkhörgâh, jadda).

sources.citation: Stilo, Donald L. 1981. The Tati language group in the sociolinguistic context of Northwestern Iran and Transcaucasia. Iranian Studies 14(3/4): 137-187. doi:10.1080/00210868108701585
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Razajerdi is placed in 'Group Seven: Dialects north and northeast of Qazvin, A. Qazvin Kuhpaye area (Razajerd, etc.)' (p. 140); Razajerdi pronoun/genitive/possessive forms appear in Table 1 and Isomaps 1-2 (pp. 150-151); p. 179 n. 3 says the Razajerdi data are from Stilo's own field notes. The word 'stress' occurs only in 'The point I wish to stress'.

sources.note: Only modern description that names Razajerdi (Glottolog cites p. 664 for its subclassification); Stilo's areal survey of Caspian and Tatic includes phonology and is the most likely place for a word-stress statement drawn from his own Razajerdi field notes.

sources.citation: Stilo, Donald L. Unpublished Razajerdi field notes (cited as the data source in Stilo 1981: 179 n. 3), and the Atlas of the Araxes-Iran Linguistic Area (AILA) materials.

sources.note: The primary data on Razajerdi exist only in Stilo's field notes; any stress statement in Stilo 2018 rests on them.

sources.citation: Varjavand, Parviz. 1349/1970. Sarzamin-e Qazvin [The land of Qazvin]. Tehran: Anjoman-e Asar-e Melli. (Persian; section on the language of Razeh-jerd/Kuhpayeh Tati, quoted on the Razjerd village website.)

sources.note: Earliest published notice specifically on the speech of Razeh-jerd (gender marking, classification as the third Kuhpayeh Tati type); may contain transcribed material with stress marks. Not found on archive.org.

sources.citation: Yar-Shater, Ehsan. 1969. A Grammar of Southern Tati Dialects (Median Dialect Studies I). The Hague: Mouton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Standard grammar of the neighbouring Southern Tati dialects (Takestani, Chali, Eshtehardi, Ramand villages) with stress discussion; Glottolog now groups Razajerdi with these (Ramand-Karaj), though Stilo 1981 kept it separate. Would show whether Razajerd was among Yar-Shater's field points. archive.org copy is controlled lending; HathiTrust search-only.
